source: ISO 32000-2:2020 as amended by Errata Collection 3
scope: Selected current assertion/source recheck of three structure-attribute tables: Table 381 columns, Table 382 list attributes, and Table 384 table-cell attributes. This is not a whole-§14.8 certificate; nearby Table 383 PrintField is cross-referenced to confirmed B29.

source_locations.text: Table381 caption/header and ColumnCount only; ColumnGap begins on physical804.
Table381 continuation: complete ColumnGap and ColumnWidths entries, including short/excess-array semantics.

effective_rule_features: When a grouping element's content is divided into columns, the Table 381 attributes shall be present.
ColumnCount is integer, optional, noninheritable, default 1.
ColumnGap may be a number or an array; short arrays repeat the last stated gap; excess elements are ignored. The cell says the array should contain numbers.

ColumnWidths may be a number or an array; short arrays repeat the last width; excess elements are ignored; values are user-space widths in inline progression and the cell requires numeric array members.
selected_tables.errata: Effective replacement Table 377 is appended at physical 1013–1014 by EC3 #223/#226 and maps these column attributes to grouping elements. Table 381 itself is physical 803–804; no direct Table 381 value correction was identified in the prior source audit.
selected_tables.ledger_and_code: Ledger §14.8.5.4.7 is classified inapplicable as a column-layout consumer. The current viewer presents the authored page content; its rendering, selection and accessibility paths do not use ColumnCount/ColumnGap/ColumnWidths to reflow content. The attributes are not claimed to be parsed into a consumer result.
selected_tables.assertions: The prior structure_layout_remaining_current source audit searched current structure/layout tests and found no assertions carrying these values into a consumer. This is expected under the current display-only scope and is not a reader defect by itself.
selected_tables.verdict: No gap established for this product path. Table cells contain layout-process instructions; the page appearance already encodes placement. No test draft: a parser-only short-array test would not validate a current supported consumer, and no reflow output contract is adopted.
residuals: If a reflow/export consumer is adopted, separately test short and excess arrays, ColumnGap versus ColumnWidths strength wording, inline progression, and default ColumnCount.

source_locations.text: §14.8.5.5 lead-in; this is context, not Table 382's caption.
Table 382 definition. ListNumbering values, default None, ordered/unordered classification and NOTE; ContinuedList/ContinuedFrom.

effective_rule_features: ListNumbering is optional and inheritable, default None; the table defines its value set and says the list is unordered unless one of the listed ordered values is present.

The NOTE permits extraction tools to autonumber, while warning that Lbl may already contain explicit results; it does not itself erase the preceding list-kind classification or require duplicate label generation.

EC3 #346 makes ContinuedList and ContinuedFrom noninheritable; it does not make ListNumbering noninheritable. The two continuation attributes have separate current implementation and consumer tests and are not retested here.
selected_tables.ledger_and_code: Current ledger row 14.8.5.5 implements continuation interpretation and marks ListNumbering inapplicable on the rationale that it is only a renumbering scheme. Current Tree/list consumer carries continuation data but no ordered/unordered classification; all standard Lists project as the generic list role.
selected_tables.assertions: No ListNumbering assertion was found in the current implementation tests. Existing continuation tests do not prove the independent ListNumbering classification. D17 records this exact source-to-consumer gap as a qualified policy/API question.
selected_tables.verdict: D17 remains open as a source-to-consumer disposition question, not an execution-confirmed mandatory reader defect. The table makes an explicit ordered/unordered distinction, but the public host vocabulary presently has one generic List role. Do not infer that labels must be regenerated or impose a platform representation without an owner decision.
residuals: Whether and how list kind is exposed to the public accessibility consumer remains unresolved. Inheritance of ListNumbering is permitted by the table but has no current consumer to exercise it.

source_locations.text: Table 384 begins: RowSpan, ColSpan, Headers and Scope.
Table 384 continuation: Summary and Short, then Table 385 begins later on this page.

effective_rule_features: RowSpan and ColSpan default to 1, are noninheritable and have effect only on TH/TD; placement follows the table's WritingMode axes.

Headers is noninheritable; explicit IDs order row headers before column headers, each most-specific-first, and recursive TH Headers contribute. If scope cannot be determined, the cited header must specify Scope.
Scope is a noninheritable TH axis classification. Summary is noninheritable and Table-only, with a nonvisual rendering note; Short is noninheritable, PDF 2.0, and TH-only.

EC3 #200 amends the §14.8.4.8.3 implicit search: an adopted search should not terminate at a TH whose Scope conflicts with its search direction, regardless of that TH's Headers. This is a SHOULD refinement of an optional algorithm, not a universal mandate to implement implicit association.
selected_tables.ledger_and_code: Current ledger §14.8.5.7 maps cell geometry/header relations and Summary/Short. `pdf-model::Tree::cell_facts` reads spans, Scope, IDs and explicit Headers; `viewer-core` places cells and resolves associations; `viewer-accessibility` delivers header names/descriptions. `table_header_conflicting_scope_spec_audit.rs` is a public Viewer/accessibility consumer test for the #200 correction.
selected_tables.assertions: Current existing model/headless/AT-SPI tests cover source-derived span defaults/placement, explicit and implicit header associations, recursive ordering, Scope role/description, Summary and Short routing. The newly promoted exact-xref public regression includes Row/Column and with/without Headers controls. Parent execution records three controls passing and the Row-with-Headers case failing with only Named, omitting eligible Middle/Far. This is B53, an adopted optional-algorithm/SHOULD gap, not a claim that all readers must use the algorithm. It does not settle whether Named also contributes or how a later TD affects termination.
selected_tables.verdict: No new distinct Table 384 defect/draft from this shard. Preserve confirmed B53 and its limits; the earlier structure_attributes shard's no-new-failure statement predates that current dedicated regression and should not be read as disposition of #200.
residuals: No whole-table certification here; B53 is limited to the public named-row-header continuation witness and leaves the issue's identified alternatives open.

explicit_exclusions.reason: Separate confirmed B29 already tests public disappearance of Role, Checked, Desc from valid exact-xref forms. It is not duplicated in this selected three-table matrix.
Distinct language/ActualText issues and consumer paths; no Table 381/382/384 cell-level overlap asserted here.

explicit_exclusions.feature: Table 378 WritingMode and Tables 379/380 layout attributes

execution: Source/assertion review only. No Cargo command was run by this shard. B53 outcomes are parent-reported from its promoted test run, not a run performed here.
